clue.text: Kingdom acquired by matricide?

parts.note: matricide is killing your mother, or to '...', and a kingdom is a realm or territory ruled over

explanation.surface: A dark tale of someone who murdered their mother to seize the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Matricide means doing in your Ma: DO + MA + IN, run together, spells a word for a realm.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm or territory under one ruler's control is a synonym for kingdom.

clue.text: See 22
Boatman thus greets one; going on theory, he waves

indicators.note: going on means placed in front of what follows, as this is a down light

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article

indicators.note: waves means shakes about, so the letters of theory and he are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boatman greets someone, waving while musing on some theory.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is also the setter's name, so the clue is the setter introducing himself. 'Waves' rearranges THEORY + HE to HOYTHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor's traditional hailing call to another vessel or person, so it is how a seafarer would greet.

clue.text: Fine pintail carried by pointer

indicators.note: in a down light, carried by means sitting on top of the next piece

parts.note: the tail, or last letter, of pin is N
an arrow is a pointer on a sign

explanation.surface: A pintail duck held up by a gun dog, a pointer, in a fine retrieve.
explanation.walkthrough: Pintail and pointer look like a duck and a gun dog; in fact 'pintail' is the tail of 'pin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine as in thin or slender, like a fine line, is a synonym.

clue.text: Hard natured? I could be improved

indicators.note: improving something changes its form, so the letters of natured and I are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone hard-hearted wonders whether they could become better natured.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardened or made firm, especially of tissue or character, is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: With it, lark perhaps rises over shore; poet likewise begins singing, but not all at once

parts.note: with it means fashionable, which is IN

indicators.note: rises means goes up, so in a down light the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a lark is an example of a bird

indicators.note: likewise says the next piece also rises, reading upwards as the bird did
begins picks the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A lark rises over the shore and a poet starts to sing, but only in fits and starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rises' turns BIRD to DRIB; 'likewise' turns BARD to DRAB too. 'With it' is IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving in small amounts over time is the idiom's meaning, so piecemeal, never all together.

clue.text: A number of years before part of the Bible becomes corrupt

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second

parts.note: a decade is ten years, a particular number of them
NT is the New Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Over many years, part of scripture goes bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Morally decayed and self-indulgent is a synonym for corrupt as an adjective.

clue.text: Revive wren horribly pecked by eagle's beak

indicators.note: being pecked by a beak puts that beak inside the rearranged wren
horribly suggests something mangled, so the letters of wren are rearranged
a beak is at the front of a bird, so this takes the first letter of eagle's

explanation.surface: An eagle attacks a small wren, which a rescuer tries to bring round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horribly' rearranges WREN to RENW, and 'pecked by' puts E, the eagle's beak, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore or resume something is a synonym for revive.

clue.text: Capsize, following report of one seen flying, a sea creature

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so this signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a tern is a seabird, seen flying
a turtle is a sea creature

explanation.surface: A boat capsizes after news of a flying bird and a sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for overturning a boat so it ends up upside down, the same as capsize.

clue.text: As said of old, did raven and dove dance and turn crimson?

indicators.note: to dance is to move about, so the letters of dove are rearranged

parts.note: a U-turn, so turn gives U
crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: The biblical flood story: Noah's raven and dove, here dancing and blushing red.
explanation.walkthrough: Raven here is the verb, rhyming with 'haven': to eat greedily. 'Dance' rearranges DOVE to DEVO. 'As said of old' just colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To raven is to eat hungrily, so did raven is the past tense synonym, gobbled up.

clue.text: One sings in cage, cautious, giving out initial warning

parts.note: can is slang for prison, a cage

indicators.note: giving out means letting go of, so a letter is dropped
initial picks the first letter of warning

explanation.surface: A caged songbird, ever cautious, gives the first alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving out' drops the W, the initial of 'warning', from WARY. 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small songbird often kept in a cage is an example of one that sings.

clue.text: See 22
Beneath cuckoo's wings (so artful, so wrong!), not about to run

indicators.note: beneath means the following piece sits under the first in this down light
wings are a bird's two sides, so the outer letters of cuckoo's
wrong means not right, so the letters of so artful are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cuckoo, so artful in laying its eggs, is wrong yet won't flee.
explanation.walkthrough: Outer letters of cuckoo (C, O) — the possessive 's ignored — then 'wrong' rearranges SO ARTFUL to LOURFAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Dye that will not fade or bleed when washed; colour that runs is the opposite, so not about to run.

clue.text: See 22
Confident about homework? That's easy!

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: split into home and work: home is IN and work gives EC

explanation.surface: A pupil, sure of their homework, declares it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homework' must be read as two words: home (IN) and work (EC), placed inside SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A paid post requiring little or no effort, an easy job, so an exclamation of ease fits.

clue.text: Spooner to control birds with old weapons

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the opening sounds trade places

explanation.surface: Spooner tries to control birds with ancient arms.
explanation.walkthrough: BOSS CROWS with starts swapped gives CROSS BOWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval missile launchers firing bolts are examples of old weapons.

clue.text: You may not imitate a bird

parts.note: to forge is to imitate fraudulently
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A firm refusal: you're not allowed to imitate a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiomatic flat refusal meaning no way, the same as saying permission is denied.

clue.text: Number 1 Queen disc Flash — it's first given a spin on AM

indicators.note: given a spin means turned round, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: number one, read as no one, gives NO ONE
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen
a disc is round, like the letter O

indicators.note: it's first picks the first letter of the word Flash

explanation.surface: A radio DJ spins Queen's number one, Flash, on AM radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given a spin' reverses NO ONE + R + O + F (Flash's first letter). Queen did have a hit called Flash.
explanation.definitionFit: AM, ante meridiem, is the morning, and the archaic word here is the morning hours.

clue.text: Headless chickens? Proverbially, the opposite

indicators.note: headless means losing the head, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: Panicking people, headless chickens, are the opposite of something proverbial.
explanation.walkthrough: Headless chickens are proverbially foolish and frantic; the birds here are proverbially wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds famed in proverbs for wisdom are the opposite of panicky, foolish headless chickens.

clue.text: Picked up fuel, one seen in flight overseas

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so a word that sounds like another

explanation.surface: Someone collects fuel while a plane flies abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: PETROL said aloud gives PETREL. 'Overseas' means over the sea, not abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird that flies far out over the ocean, so it is seen in flight over the sea.

clue.text: Scrambled eggs endorsed and used in an emergency by the army

definitions.text: used in an emergency by the army

indicators.note: scrambled means mixed up, so the letters of eggs and endorsed are rearranged

explanation.surface: Army rations: scrambled eggs, officially approved and served in emergencies.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, Green Goddesses were old army fire engines brought out when firefighters were on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A British military fire engine kept for emergencies, an example of army emergency equipment.

clue.text: One wades in with a bill, say? About time

definitions.text: One wades in with a bill

parts.note: e.g. means for example, or say

explanation.surface: Someone walks in carrying a bill, asking about the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged heron that wades in shallow water and has a long beak, so wades with a bill.

clue.text: Use a crafty throw — and, lo, siskin and tit now bleed

definitions.text: Use a crafty throw — and, lo, siskin and tit now bleed

indicators.note: crafty suggests cunning rearrangement, so the following letters are reworked

explanation.surface: One clever throw of a stone and two birds, a siskin and a tit, are bleeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' rearranges THROW, LO, SISKIN and TIT NOW BLEED; the two 'and's are links. The whole clue also pictures the saying.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for achieving two aims with one action, pictured literally by one stone hitting two birds.

clue.text: Copy section about redstart and duck

indicators.note: about means around, so part goes round the other pieces

parts.note: read as red's start, the first letter of red
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, O

explanation.surface: Part of a birding guide describes a redstart and a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: A redstart is a bird, but here it is the start of 'red'.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat words mechanically is to copy them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Samba man from Brazil broadcast in flight

parts.note: Airto Moreira is a Brazilian percussionist

explanation.surface: A Brazilian samba musician's show is broadcast on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something between aircraft, so it happens while airborne, during flight.

clue.text: Figures out the end in acts

indicators.note: in puts the picked letter inside the figures
the end picks the last letter of the word out

explanation.surface: Figuring out how acts end.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws passed by a legislature, such as acts of Parliament, are a synonym.

clue.text: Ultimately, one learns not to be horrid

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

indicators.note: not to be means the word be is removed

explanation.surface: In the end, a person learns not to be nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not to be' strips BE from BEASTLY, leaving ASTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: In the end, finally, is a synonym of this adverb.
